source.quote: Shanling's own announcement for the EC3, read 2026-11-25, with its manual at /catlog/EC3.pdf; the product page /product/425 is 19 image slices. Verbatim: « Built around well proven Philips CD80 drive mechanism and HD850 laser head, as a top-loading CD player with a transparent cover. Offering digital outputs in form of coaxial and optical SPDIF, for easy connection to external DACs or receivers. It also packs its own audio circuit, utilizing ESS ES9219C DAC and LTA8092 op-amp through headphone output or RCA »; « Allowing it to act as a Bluetooth DAC or serving as a Hi-Res music player by connecting any USB drive with audio files ». The manual's only figure sits under its heading « USB Driver Playback »: « 3. Support up to PCM 384kHz and DSD256. »

facts.chip: « ESS ES9219C DAC and LTA8092 op-amp ».

_la_source_est_une_annonce_ou_un_manuel_: Shanling's product pages are image-only, so every figure comes from the maker's own announcement at /article/NNNNNN or from its manual PDF, both on en.shanling.com. No number was read off an image, and nothing is sourced to store.shanling.com. See the brand file.
_ni_DoP_ni_natif_ne_sont_dits_pour_ce_mo: DoP appears on no Shanling page or manual, and « native » only in the UA dongle manuals and in EM5. Neither is stated for this model, so both fields are absent rather than guessed.
_le_coaxial_et_loptique_sont_des_sorties: « Offering digital outputs in form of coaxial and optical SPDIF » - outputs, said in those words. And the USB is for « connecting any USB drive with audio files », which is storage. So the ONLY digital input on this CD player is Bluetooth, and the 384 kHz / DSD256 figure describes files it reads off a stick. `pcm_max_hz` records what the device converts; `inputs` holds one key, and it is the wireless one. A harvester reading « coaxial and optical SPDIF » plus « 384kHz » would have produced two high-rate S/PDIF inputs that do not exist.
